nodes.summary: For a finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ write $A + A = \{a + b : a, b \in A\}$. For every natural number $k \ge 3$ and every real number $C \ge 2$ there is a real number $c > 0$ such that every finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $|A + A| < C|A|$ has at least $c|A|^2$ pairs $(a, d)$ of integers with $a + i d \in A$ for all natural numbers $i < k$.
nodes.title: Sets of small doubling contain many arithmetic progressions

nodes.summary: For a finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ write $A + A = \{a + b : a, b \in A\}$. This is the statement that for every natural number $k \ge 3$ and every real number $C \ge 2$ there is a real number $c > 0$ such that every finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $|A + A| < C|A|$ has at least $c|A|^2$ pairs $(a, d)$ of integers with $a + i d \in A$ for all natural numbers $i < k$.
nodes.title: Katz's question on progressions in sets of small doubling

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$ and a finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the set of pairs $(a, d)$ of integers such that $a + i d \in A$ for every natural number $i < k$. The pair $(a, d)$ stands for the $k$-term arithmetic progression $a, a + d, \dots, a + (k - 1)d$; the difference $d$ may be zero or negative.
nodes.title: Arithmetic progressions in a finite set of integers, as pairs

nodes.summary: For a finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the sumset $A + A = \{a + b : a, b \in A\}$, a finite set of integers.
nodes.title: Sumset of a finite set of integers
